neighbours.label: words of limitless or immeasurable extent (infinite, endless, billions, forever)
fire: The poet wrote of an infinite sky above the quiet desert.
Her grandmother seemed to have boundless energy every morning.
Light from billions of distant galaxies reaches the telescope.
The desert sand seemed to stretch out endlessly to the horizon.
Mathematicians proved there are infinitely many prime numbers.
The child asked whether the road goes on forever.
With limitless resources, the company could build anything.
Trillions of tiny cells make up the human body.
quiet: The poet wrote of a gray sky above the quiet desert.
Her grandmother seemed to have little energy every morning.
Light from a few nearby stars reaches the small telescope.
The desert sand seemed to stretch out for a mile to the hill.
Mathematicians proved there are exactly four such prime numbers.
The child asked whether the road goes on past the farm.
With modest resources, the company could build a small shop.
Dozens of tiny cells were visible under the microscope.

notes: top: infinite x10, infinitely x6, billions x3, Chinese 无限/无穷. Probes: endless, forever, limitless fire; 'twelve' does not.
